paths.tree: HEAD of the repo given by --repo (import graph by module stem)

summary.note: ground truth = a covers-bound test fails; candidate tests are the covers-bearing test files that name the module (textual, capped at 8 per root), so a probe the candidates could not see counts as not caught

setup.grade: plugins/shipwright-grade/tests produced a database (393 passed, 1 skipped, 225 KB) when run from the plugin directory; the 10 collection errors of the REPLAY run came from running it from the repo root (the plugin's own pyproject pythonpath/rootdir applies only from its directory)
setup.how: one pytest process per root, serial; plugin roots from the plugin directory as ci.yml does (--cov=scripts --cov=<tree>/shared); shared roots and integration-tests from the repo root with -m 'not slow and not cross_plugin' for the three shared roots; --cov-context=test; test ids and file paths root-prefixed at load time (prefix_of + load_contexts)
setup.not_measured: shared roots measure only shared; a plugin's scripts are measured in that plugin's root only (not in shared/integration roots)

shared_tests_failures_17.reading: 0 failures in a clean detached worktree at both the REPLAY-time commit (13397 passed = 17 + 13380, the same test count) and current main, with the same --cov-context=test run and the same scrubbed environment. So the 17 are not commit-dependent and not caused by the context run; they came from the state of the checkout the REPLAY run used (working tree with the BL0 files and other local state). Their names were not stored, so which tests they were, and whether they were FR-bound, cannot be recovered; not reproducible.

setup.tool: uv run --with coverage shared/scripts/tools/bl0b_head_run.py --tree <detached worktree at the commit> --out <dir outside it>

ac_level.note: the author declares FRs, never ACs, so a declared scope approves all ACs of an FR: the AC-level hold equals the FR-level hold by construction; the AC level changes the size of what an approval covers, not who is held
